title: Multimodal Large Language Models Predict Urban Safety Perception but Encode Non-Neutral Demographic Priors
abstract: arXiv:2503.00610v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Understanding how people perceive urban environments is essential for inclusive planning, yet conventional surveys are costly and difficult to scale. We investigate whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can assess perceived urban safety from street-view imagery while accounting for the observer-dependent nature of perception. Using Place Pulse 2.0, we evaluate four open and proprietary MLLMs across 56 cities under a Neutral prompt and socio-demographic personas defined by gender, age, and race or ethnicity. We also analyse the keywords generated to justify each classification. However, they systematically favour the Safe class, underpredict unsafety, and compress differences between cities. translated_title: 多模态大语言模型能够预测城市安全感知，但编码了非中性的人口统计学先验
translated_abstract: 理解人们如何感知城市环境对于包容性规划至关重要，然而传统调查成本高昂且难以规模化。我们研究多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）能否从街景图像中评估城市安全感知，同时考虑感知依赖于观察者这一特性。基于Place Pulse 2.0数据集，我们在56个城市中评估了四个开源与专有MLLMs，分别采用中性提示词以及由性别、年龄和种族或族裔定义的社会人口学角色设定，并分析了模型为每次分类生成的解释性关键词。结果表明，四个模型均展现出可比的零样本能力，城市宏观F1分数为65-69%，并保留了有意义的跨城市差异。然而，它们系统性地偏向“安全”类别，低估不安全性，并压缩了城市之间的差异。其解释收敛于一套共享的视觉词汇：维护状况、绿化、秩序等。
tldr: 多模态大语言模型能从街景图像零样本预测城市安全感知（城市宏观F1达65-69%），但其预测受性别、年龄、种族等社会人口学角色设定的影响，编码了非中性的人口先验，并系统性地偏向“安全”判断。
en_tdlr: Multimodal large language models zero-shot predict urban safety perception from street-view imagery (city-macro F1 of 65-69%), but encode non-neutral demographic priors, as their predictions vary with gender, age, and race personas while systematically favoring the "Safe" class.
